prerequisites: Install Instrilo v0.2.3 or newer from a release. Check instrilo --version, then prepare the tutorial workspace as shown below.
Use Bash on macOS/Linux or WSL, inside your prepared tutorial workspace. Keep every step in the same terminal.
Use a fresh tutorial project name. If init/create says the project already exists, choose a new slug and update INSTRILO_PROJECT; do not delete work you want to keep.

next.label: Inspect the tutorial fixtures and checks

title: Give builder, runtime and judge separate connections
summary: Exercise API-key, bearer and OAuth gateway connections with real local HTTP and no paid model calls.
outcome: Three independently assigned connections, a builder plan, a runtime result and a saved synthetic evaluation.

verification.scope: Actual HTTP requests, API-key and bearer headers, an OAuth client-credentials exchange, builder JSON parsing, generated runtime execution and judge report parsing all run against the documented local fixture. The bundled verify.mjs helper only reads saved JSON and asserts the expected results.
limitations: The deterministic fixture checks integration behavior, not model intelligence or response quality.
No paid model account, real credentials or cloud resource is used. Package installation still needs registry access.
The OAuth token is a plain demonstration string. This does not verify signed JWT validation, external identity-provider policy, model entitlement or production gateway behavior.
The fixture judge tests one literal phrase. Its score is not quality evidence and the dataset remains synthetic.

steps.title: Create the connection sandbox
steps.body: Each named connection is imported separately and assigned to one role. Secrets are referenced through environment variable names; the values below are public dummy tutorial strings.
steps.code:
set -eu
INSTRILO_PROJECT=.studio/tutorials/independent-model-connections
instrilo init independent-model-connections --directory .studio/tutorials
export INSTRILO_TUTORIAL_API_KEY=tutorial-api-key
export INSTRILO_TUTORIAL_CLIENT_ID=tutorial-client
export INSTRILO_TUTORIAL_CLIENT_SECRET=tutorial-client-secret
test -f "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/agent-studio.yaml"
steps.expected: The project exists. Only dummy local credentials are set.

steps.title: Start the named local demonstration service
steps.body: This bundled helper runs on an available localhost port. It returns deterministic model replies and synthetic order data. It is a demonstration service, not a real LLM. The EXIT trap stops only its tracked process if a later command fails.
steps.code:
node examples/quickstarts/foundations/fixture.mjs serve "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture.json" > "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture.log" 2>&1 &
INSTRILO_FIXTURE_PID=$!
trap 'kill "$INSTRILO_FIXTURE_PID" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
node examples/quickstarts/foundations/fixture.mjs wait "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture.json"
node examples/quickstarts/foundations/fixture.mjs files "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture.json" "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/connections"
export INSTRILO_TUTORIAL_BEARER=tutorial-bearer
steps.expected: The helper prints “Local deterministic fixture is ready” and writes five JSON connection/tool documents containing its actual local port.

steps.title: Assign each role explicitly
steps.body: The fixture helper writes inspectable JSON with the actual ephemeral URL. Builder uses the OpenAI-compatible API format plus an API-key environment reference; runtime uses a custom gateway with bearer authentication; judge uses client credentials with scope and audience.
steps.code:
cat "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/connections/builder.json" "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/connections/runtime.json" "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/connections/judge.json"
instrilo connections add planning "$INSTRILO_PROJECT" --file "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/connections/builder.json"
instrilo connections add answering "$INSTRILO_PROJECT" --file "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/connections/runtime.json"
instrilo connections add scoring "$INSTRILO_PROJECT" --file "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/connections/judge.json"
instrilo connections use builder planning "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
instrilo connections use runtime answering "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
instrilo connections use judge scoring "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
instrilo connections list "$INSTRILO_PROJECT" > "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/roles.json"
cat "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/roles.json"
node examples/quickstarts/foundations/verify.mjs roles "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
steps.expected: The role map names planning, answering and scoring. The stored documents contain environment-variable names, not secret values.

steps.title: Ask the builder, build and run
steps.body: The plan response comes from the fixture builder. Plan without --apply is review-only. The copied case stays explicitly synthetic.
steps.code:
instrilo plan "$INSTRILO_PROJECT" > "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/plan.json"
node examples/quickstarts/foundations/verify.mjs builder "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
cp examples/quickstarts/foundations/role-cases.jsonl "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/evals/cases.jsonl"
instrilo build "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
instrilo prepare "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
instrilo run "$INSTRILO_PROJECT" --input 'When can I return an item?' > "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/run.json"
node examples/quickstarts/foundations/verify.mjs runtime "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
steps.expected: Builder JSON is accepted and the generated runtime returns the fixture’s 30-day answer.

steps.title: Call the separate judge and inspect evidence
steps.body: The runtime runs the case, then the judge obtains a local OAuth token and scores the result. The counters prove each role used its intended route.
steps.code:
instrilo eval "$INSTRILO_PROJECT" --split development --output "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/evaluation.json" > "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/eval-output.json"
node examples/quickstarts/foundations/verify.mjs evaluation "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
node examples/quickstarts/foundations/fixture.mjs stats "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture.json" > "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture-stats.json"
cat "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture-stats.json"
node examples/quickstarts/foundations/verify.mjs role-requests "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
steps.expected: One synthetic case passes. The service counts one builder request, two runtime requests, one judge request and at least one token exchange.

steps.title: Stop the fixture you started
steps.body: Keep the generated project and evidence. Stop only this tutorial process; no broad process matching or machine cleanup is needed.
steps.code:
kill "$INSTRILO_FIXTURE_PID"
wait "$INSTRILO_FIXTURE_PID" || true
trap - EXIT
printf 'Tutorial fixture stopped. Project files are retained.
'
steps.expected: The fixture stops and project files remain in .studio/tutorials.

steps.title: Adapt the connection documents for a real gateway
steps.body: For a real account, replace baseUrl and model with your provider’s actual values and put credentials in the named environment variables outside source control. bearer-env can forward an existing JWT; the gateway must validate it and enforce authorization. oauth-client-credentials requests a token with configured scope and audience; the identity provider decides what claims and permissions it grants. Separately, security.inbound configures signed JWT verification for callers of the generated agent. These are distinct boundaries. No live-account command is included in the verified steps.
steps.code:
instrilo connections example gateway
instrilo explain security
instrilo explain connections
steps.expected: The CLI prints a connection template and explains outbound gateway authentication separately from inbound agent JWT enforcement.

troubleshooting: If preparation cannot reach npm/PyPI, fix registry/proxy access and repeat prepare; it does not require model credentials.
If the project already exists, inspect or keep it and choose a new tutorial slug. Do not rerun init over an existing manifest.
If fixture readiness times out, read this project’s fixture.log. The service listens only on 127.0.0.1 and selects a free port.
Do not reuse connection files after stopping the fixture; their port is temporary. Use a fresh project to rerun the complete walkthrough.
cleanup: The final cleanup step stops the single fixture PID. Reports and generated files remain for inspection.
